 사진 확대 Photo | Star Today DB As actor Go Kyung-pyo faces controversy over a drunk-driving accident, the team behind tvN variety show Sixth Sense: B-Side has also finally decided to edit him out.
 On the 14th, the team behind Sixth Sense: B-Side told Star Today, regarding Go Kyung-pyo’s drunk-driving accident, “We plan to edit his appearances as much as possible in tomorrow’s (the 15th) broadcast and next week’s finale of Sixth Sense: B-Side so viewers can watch without discomfort.”
 Go Kyung-pyo is currently a regular cast member on Sixth Sense: B-Side. Since the accident happened with just two episodes left before the program ends, the production team has had to rush to edit the footage. The key question is how naturally they can remove Go from episodes that have already been filmed.
 Earlier, MBC’s Hangout with Yoo, which was scheduled to air that day, also said it would edit Go Kyung-pyo’s scenes as much as possible. Go had been set to appear in the “’95 Seoul Music Festival” segment, but news of the drunk-driving accident put the show in the unprecedented position of having to edit him out just before broadcast.
 At around 3:30 a.m. that day, Go Kyung-pyo was driving a passenger car after drinking in Donggyo-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul, when he collided with a street sweeper. A police alcohol test found that his blood alcohol concentration was at a level that would result in revocation of his driver’s license. After being questioned by police, Go went home, while his agency, CLN Company, acknowledged the accident and apologized.
 The fallout from the accident is not limited to programs currently on air. Go Kyung-pyo is also scheduled to appear on tvN’s The Village Barber 2 and TVING’s The Great Escape: Urban Legends, both set to premiere on the 29th. A fan meeting is also scheduled for the 21st at Seongam Art Hall in Seoul, and substantial disruption to his future activities is expected to be inevitable.
 [Shin Young-eun, Star Today reporter]
